activity_context.topic_title: Changing the Order of Integration in Double Integrals

examples.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Double Integral by Swapping the Order of Integration
examples.problem: Change the order of integration and evaluate the double integral $\displaystyle{\int_0^{1} \int_{\sqrt{x}}^{1 } 9\sqrt{y^3+1}\,\textrm{d}y\,\textrm{d}x}.$
examples.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/1045aaad8025b20309b92477b4a1cf98e138064210c6fbc960c64ec26c9951df.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. This is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D = \big\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \quad \sqrt{x} \leq y \leq 1 \big\}.
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
x=0,
$$

and the right boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y = \sqrt{x} 
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
x=y^2.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as type II region. Its type II representation is

$$
D = \big\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \quad 0 \leq x \leq y^2 \big\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/40cbaaff270daddf4b60115cc272fbc8b165b83b8823d19de2c19802617ebdb4.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{x}}^{1}9\sqrt{{y}^{3}+1}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}9\sqrt{{y}^{3}+1}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =9{\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{{y}^{3}+1}[{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}y \\  & =9{\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{{y}^{3}+1}[x\,]_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\,dy \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{1}3{y}^{2}({y}^{3}+1)^{1/2}\,dy \\  & =3{[\frac{2}{3}({y}^{3}+1)^{3/2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =[2({y}^{3}+1)^{3/2}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =2(2)^{3/2}-2 \\  & =4\sqrt{2}-2.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Change the order of integration in the double integral 
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x-1}^{\sqrt{1-x}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/0e338b779e846bc3f5ac981c93f9cda65b63d654c1152aa423f855d12d7978d9.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. This is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,x-1\le y\le \sqrt{1-x}}.
$$

To change the order of integration, we need to split $D$ into two type II regions. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/d2d1df8652af81fbcb789ac05a2d1bf43f9b5b12f394159d0eb17b4ecec90042.png)

Notice that the right boundary of the lower region, written in the form $x=x(y),$  is 

$\,$ $x=y+1.$

Also, the right boundary of the upper region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$\,$ $x=1-{y}^{2}.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le y\le 0,\,0\le x\le y+1}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,0\le x\le 1-{y}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x-1}^{\sqrt{1-x}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{y+1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-{y}^{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
